targetAudience.primary: Engineers designing digital-employee and agent workflow runtimes
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands asynchronous tasks, workflow completion and error propagation.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A parent workflow can report success while detached work it still owns remains active or has failed.

whyNow: A same-day merged Google ADK change makes tracked in-flight detached dynamic work participate in enclosing workflow terminal truth.

externalHook.description: Returning from the foreground path is not proof that all work owned by the workflow is terminal.

coreProposition: Detached work must remain part of parent workflow terminal truth until it reaches a governed terminal state or its ownership is explicitly transferred; foreground return and static-graph completion are not sufficient terminal evidence.

originalValue.description: Reframes background-task correctness around ownership and terminal evidence, while separating local lifecycle closure from external-effect certainty.

readerTakeaway: Maintain stable identities for owned detached work, join and inspect it before parent success, and model transfer, cancellation and crash recovery as distinct governed outcomes.

supported: The merged ADK path waits for tracked in-flight detached dynamic tasks after static work completes.
Raised exceptions, returned child errors and non-resumable detached interrupts can prevent clean parent success.
Focused tests cover in-flight detached success, failure and interrupt outcomes.
uncertain: How already-finished detached runs should be distinguished from awaited work
How cancellation should affect parent terminal truth

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article establishes a general workflow-terminal accounting pattern without a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged mechanism and focused tests support a precise ownership-based terminal-truth conclusion with explicit limits.
